title: Access Management: Conditional Access and Roles

header.html: Describe Microsoft Entra Conditional Access; Describe Microsoft Entra roles and role-based access control (RBAC)
the official SC-900 study guide, skills measured as of October 21, 2026

html:
1Microsoft Entra Conditional Access

Conditional Access is the policy engine of Zero Trust. It makes if-then decisions at sign-in: if certain signals are true, then apply a decision.

Signals (the "if") Decisions (the "then")
User or group Block access
Location (country or IP range) Grant access
Device (platform, compliant, managed) Grant but require MFA
Application being accessed Require a compliant or hybrid-joined device
Sign-in risk and user risk (from ID Protection) Require an approved app, a password change or terms of use
Client app (browser, legacy protocols) Session controls, such as limited access or sign-in frequency

Key facts:

  • Conditional Access needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher; risk-based conditions need P2. [Verify live]
  • Policies can run in report-only mode to test the effect before enforcing them.
  • Exclude emergency access (break-glass) accounts so an administrator cannot be locked out by mistake.
  • Conditional Access is evaluated after the first factor (the user has signed in with the first method).
  • Security defaults are the free alternative; they cannot be used together with Conditional Access policies.

Typical policies: require MFA for all users, require MFA for administrators, block legacy authentication, require a compliant device for corporate apps, block sign-in from certain countries.

Exam tip

. "If the user is outside the office then require MFA" = Conditional Access. It is identity-driven policy and it needs P1. Report-only mode tests a policy without enforcing it.

Exam tip

. Global Administrator can do everything, so keep very few and protect them with MFA. Other tasks need the narrowest role (least privilege).

2Microsoft Entra roles

Microsoft Entra roles (also called directory roles or administrator roles) give people the permissions to manage Microsoft Entra resources, such as users, groups and applications.

Built-in role What it can do
Global Administrator Everything in Entra ID and connected Microsoft services; use very few
User Administrator Manage users and groups and reset passwords
Security Administrator Manage security features and read security information
Global Reader Read everything, change nothing
Conditional Access Administrator Manage Conditional Access policies

Use the least-privilege principle: give people the narrowest role that lets them do their job, and keep the number of Global Administrators small (and protected with MFA).

3Role-based access control (RBAC)

Role-based access control (RBAC) grants access by role instead of by person. A role assignment has three parts:

Part Meaning
Security principal Who: a user, group, service principal or managed identity
Role definition What: a collection of permissions
Scope Where: the resource, resource group, subscription or management group

Two role systems

Microsoft Entra roles Azure RBAC
Manages access to Microsoft Entra resources (users, groups, apps) Azure resources (VMs, storage, networks)
Scope Tenant, administrative unit, or an object Management group, subscription, resource group, resource
Example roles Global Administrator, User Administrator Owner, Contributor, Reader

Azure RBAC built-in roles: Owner (full access and can assign roles), Contributor (create and manage resources, cannot assign roles), Reader (view only).

Exam tip

. Entra roles = manage identities. Azure RBAC = manage Azure resources. Owner can assign roles; Contributor cannot. Least privilege is the principle behind both. Assign roles to groups rather than individuals where possible.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants to require MFA only when a user signs in from outside the country. Which feature fits?

  • ASelf-service password reset
  • BAzure Firewall
  • CA sensitivity label
  • DConditional Access
Show the answer

Answer: D. Conditional Access applies if-then rules using signals such as location.

S2Before enforcing a new Conditional Access policy, the team wants to see its effect without blocking anyone. What should it use?

  • AA Global Administrator account
  • BReport-only mode
  • CPassword writeback
  • DFederation
Show the answer

Answer: B. Report-only mode evaluates a policy and logs the result without enforcing it.

S3Which role should be given to a person who only needs to reset user passwords?

  • AUser Administrator
  • BGlobal Administrator
  • COwner of the subscription
  • DGlobal Reader
Show the answer

Answer: A. Least privilege means the narrowest role that fits, such as User Administrator.

S4A user needs to create virtual machines in a resource group but must not assign roles to others. Which Azure RBAC role fits?

  • AOwner
  • BReader
  • CGlobal Administrator
  • DContributor
Show the answer

Answer: D. Contributor can create and manage resources but cannot assign roles.

S5Which statement describes Microsoft Entra roles?

  • AThey manage virtual machines, storage accounts and virtual networks in Azure subscriptions and resource groups
  • BThey replace Conditional Access policies and remove the need for any MFA settings
  • CThey encrypt data at rest in storage accounts and databases using customer keys
  • DThey give permissions to manage Microsoft Entra resources such as users and applications
Show the answer

Answer: D. Entra roles control administration of identity resources, while Azure RBAC controls Azure resources.

S6Which part of an RBAC role assignment states where the permissions apply?

  • ASecurity principal
  • BRole definition
  • CToken
  • DScope
Show the answer

Answer: D. The scope says where, such as a subscription or resource group.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What does Conditional Access do?

Show the answer

Makes if-then access decisions at sign-in using signals.

R2Which license level does Conditional Access need?

Show the answer

Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher.

R3Name three Conditional Access decisions.

Show the answer

For example block, grant, require MFA, require a compliant device.

R4What are the three parts of a role assignment?

Show the answer

Security principal, role definition and scope.

R5Which Azure RBAC role can assign roles?

Show the answer

Owner.

R6Why exclude emergency access accounts from policies?

Show the answer

So administrators cannot be locked out by a mistake.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Conditional Access if-then at sign-in; signals (user, location, device, app, risk); decisions (block, grant, MFA, compliant device); P1; report-only mode
Entra roles manage identity resources; Global Administrator (few), User Administrator, Security Administrator, Global Reader
RBAC principal + role definition + scope; Azure roles Owner, Contributor, Reader; least privilege
Two systems Entra roles = identities; Azure RBAC = Azure resources
